cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and gives him an assignment: "Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites." Then He tells Moses what comes after that.

cards.question: After Moses takes vengeance on the Midianites, what does the LORD say will happen to him?

answers.text: He will be gathered to his people
He will cross over the Jordan
He will be made king of Israel

cards.text: So Moses tells the people to arm some of their men to go execute the LORD's vengeance on Midian. Not the whole camp, though. He's got a number in mind.

cards.question: Moses says to send into battle a ___ men from each tribe of Israel.
A thousand men from each tribe of Israel makes an army of twelve thousand armed for war.

cards.text: Moses sends them into battle, and with them goes Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest. Phinehas doesn't show up empty-handed.

cards.question: What does Phinehas take with him into battle?

answers.text: The sanctuary vessels and signal trumpets
The ark of the covenant and Aaron's staff
The priestly robes and the anointing oil

cards.text: They wage war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they kill every male. Among the slain are Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian, plus one more name you might remember from earlier in Numbers.

cards.question: Besides the five kings of Midian, who else is killed with the sword?

cards.text: The Israelites capture the Midianite women and their children. They take all the herds, the flocks and the goods too.

cards.question: With the people and goods taken, what do the Israelites do to the Midianite cities and encampments?
The army carries away all the plunder, both people and animals. Where do they bring it?

answers.text: To Moses at the camp in Moab

cards.text: Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the leaders go out to meet them outside the camp. But Moses is angry with the officers, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.

cards.question: Moses is angry with the army's officers. What does he ask them?

answers.text: If they spared all the women
Why they killed the five kings
Where Phinehas had gone off to

cards.text: Moses points back to Peor, in Numbers 25. He says these women, through the counsel of Balaam, the man Balak king of Moab once called to curse Israel (Numbers 22:5-6), caused the sons of Israel to turn unfaithfully against the LORD.

cards.question: Moses says that because of what happened at Peor, a ___ struck the congregation of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses gives a hard order: kill all the boys, and every woman who has had relations with a man. Every girl who never has is to be spared.
The soldiers are back from Midian, but they can't just stroll into camp. Moses says anyone who has killed a person or touched the dead has to stay outside the camp first.

cards.question: How long must anyone who has killed a person or touched the dead stay outside the camp?
On the third day and the seventh day, the soldiers purify themselves and their captives too.

cards.text: Moses adds every garment, leather good, goat's hair item and wooden article to the cleanup list. Then Eleazar the priest shares the LORD's statute for the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin and lead.

cards.question: Eleazar says the metal that can withstand the fire is made clean how?

answers.text: It is buried for seven days
It is offered on the altar

cards.text: Anything that can take the heat goes through the fire. Friend, I have been saying that about cookie dough for YEARS.

cards.question: Eleazar also has a rule for everything that can't withstand the fire. What happens to it?

answers.text: It must pass through the water
It must be burned outside the camp
It must be left behind in Midian

cards.text: Even the metal that went through the fire still gets the water of purification. On the seventh day the soldiers wash their clothes, they're clean, and they can come back into camp.
Then the LORD tells Moses, Eleazar the priest and the family heads to count everything captured, both people and animals. After that, they're to divide it into two halves.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to divide the captives into two halves. Who gets them?

answers.text: The soldiers and the rest of the congregation
The Levites and the twelve tribes of Israel
The commanders and the heads of the families

cards.question: From the soldiers' half, the tribute for the LORD is one out of every ___ persons or animals.
Who receives the tribute from the soldiers' half as an offering to the LORD?
From the congregation's half, one out of every fifty goes to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD.

cards.text: Moses and Eleazar do as the LORD commanded and count it all: 675,000 sheep, 72,000 cattle, 61,000 donkeys and 32,000 women. They split it in half, with the LORD's tribute and the Levites' share set aside, just as the LORD said.
Then the commanders of thousands and of hundreds come to Moses with a report. They've counted every soldier under their command.

cards.question: After counting the soldiers under their command, how many do the commanders say are missing?

cards.text: Not one. Every soldier accounted for. Friend, I can't get through ONE batch without losing a chocolate chip under the oven.

cards.question: The commanders bring the LORD an offering of the gold each man acquired. What do they say it's for?

answers.text: To pay for the army's weapons
To thank Moses for leading them

cards.text: Moses and Eleazar receive all the gold articles, and they weigh 16,750 shekels. On top of that, each soldier had taken plunder for himself.

cards.question: Where do Moses and Eleazar bring the commanders' gold, as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD?

answers.text: Up to the top of Mount Nebo
Across to the city of Jericho

findings.problem: The Midianites appear on the opening card without being introduced. The passage also starts in the middle of a thought, because the vengeance points back to events the baker hasn't heard about yet, and the card gives no context for it. The opening card should at least say simply who the Midianites are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question reads "a ___ men." The wrong answer "ten thousand" doesn't fit after "a" ("a ten thousand men"), so it stands apart from the other two words and helps point to the right answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question asks "Where?" but the right answer is a person plus a place ("To Moses at the camp in Moab"). The wrong answers are places only. Moses is the obvious name in the story, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card says Balak was king of Moab and cites Numbers 22:5-6. Balak's title as king of Moab comes from Numbers 22:4, so the reference should be Numbers 22:4-6.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in stop 1 (cards 1, 8, 10, 13 and 17) are flat retellings with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. A joke may not suit this material, but the cards still need his storyteller's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card only restates the answer to card 5 (fire for the metals) and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This story card only restates the answer to card 16 ("Not one. Every soldier accounted for.") and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Cards 11, 12 and 13 are all choice cards about the tribute rules in Numbers 31:28-30: the one-in-500 rate, Eleazar receiving the tribute as an offering, and the one-in-50 share for the Levites. These are rules for an offering, which is a listed kind of long stretch. The stretch should be summed up on one story card.

rule.text: rules for offerings and feasts ... A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: "On top of that, each soldier had taken plunder for himself" tells the baker how verse 53 connects to the commanders' gold. Numbers 31:53 only says each soldier had taken plunder for himself and leaves the connection open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The purification instructions in Numbers 31:19-24 get four choice cards (2, 3, 5 and 7) and several story cards. These verses are mostly detail about ritual cleansing, which could make them a long stretch. They could also be treated as the narrative's next movement.
findings.question: Do the purification statutes in Numbers 31:19-24 count as a long stretch to sum up in one story card, or as key laws that can get choice cards?

findings.problem: This passage includes the killing of every male and the order to kill the boys and the non-virgin women (Numbers 31:7, 17-18). The docs don't say how Papa Dorin should handle morally hard content. They don't say whether he should add any framing or tone beyond calling it "a hard order," or whether jokes like the ones on stop 2 cards 6 and 17 belong anywhere in a passage like this.
findings.question: How should Papa Dorin's voice and humor handle passages with violent or morally hard content like Numbers 31? Should jokes be left out entirely, and should he frame the hard orders in any way?
